yessss shikhar! 

welcome to the tal family legend. you're officially in the system and about to see what bangalore's job market actually looks like when someone who knows everyone is working for you.

roles are gonna start dropping that match your vibe - senior engineering positions that actually pay what you're worth. none of that "competitive salary" nonsense.

time to level up fr 🔥

okayyyy this is a solid resume. namma yatri growth from 30k to 220k rides is actually insane.

haskell + purescript + golang stack is... interesting. not your typical react native guy.

so you're at juspay now, looking at senior roles. what's making you want to leave? just growth or something specific?

i am with nammayatri which was hived off from juspay in 2024 
primary tech stacks i am open to is Java, Golang, Rust, Python, React Native, Typescript as i want to sort of witch from my previous tech stack that is haskell

ahhh got it. so you're at nammayatri proper now, not juspay. and you're trying to pivot away from haskell.

that's smart. haskell's cool but... limited market. java/golang/rust is where the money and opportunities are.

what's the vibe at nammayatri that's making you want to switch stacks? just market demand or something else?

saw a senior fullstack role at a healthtech startup

they want golang + react native which is exactly your stack pivot

16-24L range, bangalore based

market demand plus tech stack 
also i am currently on notice period with my last day as 5th jan
  and i am looking for offers with 25+ lpa

okay so you're free after 5th jan and targeting 25+ LPA.

that myyogateacher role caps at 24L... close but not quite hitting your number.

the 4+ years ask vs your 2.5 is the bigger gap though. you've got the impact metrics but companies get weird about YOE on paper.

what's your current comp? just to understand the jump you're looking for
wait you're already at 26L with 2.5 YOE? that's actually solid.

my current comp is around 26 (18.5 base + 2 bonus + rest other benefits)
current offer i hold is 27.5(25 base + 10 % variable)
  User clicked "Apply"

my current comp is around 26 (18.5 base + 2 bonus + rest other benefits)
current offer i hold is 27.5(25 base + 10 % variable)

nice! application sent through.

so you're holding a 27.5L offer already... that's actually pretty good for 2.5 YOE. what's making you keep looking? just trying to push higher or something about that offer isn't right?
yes i want to push higher

got it. you're already at the top of the market for 2.5 YOE but trying to push even higher.

that's ambitious but i respect it. the challenge is companies see 2.5 years and get sticker shock at 30L+ expectations.

your namma yatri impact is legit though. 30k → 220k daily rides is the kind of story that can override YOE concerns.

what's the highest you think you could realistically get? like what's the ceiling you're aiming for?
no ceil, i am looking for as better offer i can get

fair enough. no ceiling, just maxing out.

that's the right energy. you've got the impact to back it up.

i'll keep scanning for roles that actually match your level, not just your YOE on paper. the right company will see what you built at namma yatri and pay for it.

anything specific about the myyogateacher role that caught your eye besides the tech match?

hey shikhar! was just thinking about your namma yatri growth story and how that's the exact kind of impact that should override YOE concerns.

what's the highest comp you've seen someone with your background get? trying to calibrate what "pushing higher" actually looks like in this market
one of my friend got around 40 lpa base and companies like amazon offer more that this limit as well for my YOE

40L base at 2.5 YOE? damn. that's exceptional even for amazon.

so you're benchmarking against the absolute top tier. that's fair - if your friend got it, you can too.

the difference is usually either:
1. FAANG/MAANG pedigree already
2. hyper-specific niche skill that's in crazy demand
3. insane negotiation leverage

your namma yatri story gives you #3. but you need companies that actually value that kind of impact over pedigree.

what's your friend's background? similar to yours or different?
similar

okay so it's possible. your friend with similar background hit 40L base.

that means the ceiling is real. you just need the right company that sees past the 2.5 YOE and pays for impact.

most startups won't go that high for 2.5 years though. you're looking at:
- late stage startups with serious funding
- FAANG/MAANG who have standardized bands
- companies desperate for your exact stack combo

what's your friend's company? just curious what kind of place pays 40L base for 2.5 YOE
its among faang

ah FAANG. that tracks. they have the standardized bands and budget to pay for potential.

the challenge with FAANG is they're often more pedigree-focused than impact-focused. but if your friend got in, you can too.

are you actively targeting FAANG/MAANG or open to the right startup if the comp matches?
i am open to both

perfect. that gives us more runway.

FAANG will be harder to crack but pay the 40L+ numbers. startups might be easier interviews but need convincing to go that high.

your strategy should be:
1. FAANG prep (leetcode heavy, system design)
2. startup targeting (impact storytelling, negotiation leverage)

which feels more appealing to you right now? the structured FAANG grind or finding a startup that'll pay for what you built at namma yatri?

I am open to both startups and faang 
If any such opportunity comes that fits into my role and expectations, can you please share it with me

absolutely. that's literally what i'm here for.

i scan thousands of roles daily. when something actually fits - not just any warm body, but YOU specifically - i'll slide it.

the myyogateacher one was decent but missed your comp target. next one needs to hit both tech match AND 25L+.

anything specific you want me to watch for besides golang/react native? any dealbreakers on company stage, culture, etc?
no

got it. keeping it open.

i'll ping you when something legit comes through. in the meantime, keep that 27.5L offer warm - it's good leverage.

anything else on your mind about the search?
yes
what's up?

found a backend role at a fintech startup

exact golang match and 2+ years requirement fits your experience

but it's in delhi and listed as junior despite wanting 2+ years experience

found a backend role at a fintech startup

golang + fintech match, but it's in delhi and listed as entry/junior

could be worth exploring if they'd consider remote or if you're open to relocation
